subject: Intro to GridShift finance owner & next procurement steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Carter <liz.carter@gridshift.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@gridshift.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T15:12:00Z
Subject: Follow-up & ask: who signs on budget for platform spend?

Hi Liz / Tom —

Great to meet earlier — appreciate the walkthrough of your platform roadmap and where inference cost predictability matters for GridShift. Quick notes and a concrete ask:

- Summary of what we discussed: low-latency inference for near-real-time forecasting, contract flexibility for pilot -> production, and strong telemetry for cost attribution.
- Next steps we proposed: 1) short pilot (4–6 weeks) on dedicated capacity, 2) security questionnaire from your team, 3) a one-page mutual action plan to align milestones and success metrics.

Ask: can you confirm who in your org is the primary budget owner for this project (finance owner / approving manager)? That will help us prepare a tailored SOW and an internal pricing outline. If it helps, our guess from the convo is either Maria Lopez (CFO) or the Head of Platform — but we don’t want to jump to conclusions.

I’ve attached a draft SOW outline and our standard security questionnaire to give procurement visibility.

If you’d like, we can set a 30-minute call next week to loop in whomever handles budget approvals — happy to keep it very focused.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: Redwood-Initial-SOW-v0.2.pdf (PDF, 48KB); security-questionnaire-gridshift.xlsx (XLSX, 28KB)
From: Liz Carter <liz.carter@gridshift.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@gridshift.com>, procurement@gridshift.com
Date: 2027-04-19T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up & ask: who signs on budget for platform spend?

Thanks, Priyom — good recap.

Short answers:
- We like the pilot approach; security questionnaire looks fine at a glance.
- Budget owner: primary approver is Maria Lopez (CFO). Maria generally signs off on platform/infra spend > $50k. For pilots we typically route through the Head of Platform for technical sign-off and then finance for approval.
- Procurement: looping procurement here (procurement@gridshift.com) — Tom handles the initial procurement checklist and contract intake.

Could you share a 1-page cost outline for the pilot (monthly run-rate estimate + peak provisioning note)? That will accelerate internal review.

Also, Maria is traveling this week but back Mon 4/26; if you can tentatively block a short review window the week of 4/26 that would help.

Liz
Head of Platform | GridShift Energy
From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@gridshift.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@gridshift.com
Date: 2027-04-19T10:17:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up & ask: who signs on budget for platform spend?

Priyom / Karthik —

A couple procurement notes to speed things up:
- We require a brief vendor security attestation and proof of SOC2 or equivalent controls before procurement opens a PO. The attached questionnaire is a good start.
- Typical timeline from intake to PO is 2–3 weeks for pilots, longer if legal redlines the MSA.
- Please send the cost sheet and any standard MSA we should expect. If you have a pre-signed MSA that covers pilots, include it.

I’ll create a procurement intake ticket once we have the SOW + cost sheet.

Tom
Procurement Manager | GridShift Energy
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Carter <liz.carter@gridshift.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@gridshift.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-20T18:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up & ask: who signs on budget for platform spend?

Thanks Liz / Tom — that’s perfect. Attached: a one-page cost outline for a 6-week pilot (two capacity profiles: baseline and burst), our draft SOW (v0.2) and a redline-friendly MSA link.

Highlights in the cost sheet: expected token/embedding run-rate, a pilot discount line, and optional dedicated capacity add-on. We called out a conservative estimate for peak provisioning so finance has visibility to worst-case spend during testing.

Proposed next steps:
1) You create a procurement intake ticket (Tom) so we have a tracking ID.
2) If you can, confirm Maria Lopez as the finance approver — we’ll prepare a 1-pager specifically for her (financial impact, measurable success criteria).
3) Tentatively block 30 minutes the week of 4/26 for a brief decision-readout with Maria + Liz + Tom + Karthik / Priyom.

Happy to tailor the one-pager — what level of detail does Maria usually expect? High-level savings estimates and CAPEX/OPEX split or a simple pilot cost + ROI statement?

Best,
Priyom

Attachments: Redwood-Initial-SOW-v0.2.pdf; Redwood-Pilot-Costs-1page.pdf; Redwood-MSA-v1-link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=MSA-v1-redwood
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@gridshift.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Liz Carter <liz.carter@gridshift.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@gridshift.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up & ask: who signs on budget for platform spend?

Hi all — Liz looped me in. I’m the approving finance owner for platform projects of this nature.

Quick guidance on what I need to see before a pilot PO:
- One-page summary: total pilot cost, expected benefit (qualitative + any measurable metric), and what success looks like at pilot end.
- Vendor security posture: SOC2 or equivalent, and a completed security questionnaire (we review high-level controls).
- Contingency/exit terms: what happens if we stop after pilot.

If you can send the one-pager and the security questionnaire by EOD 4/23, I’ll review and aim to approve the pilot PO the following week. We can do the 20–30 minute call the week of 4/26; Liz, please coordinate.

Regards,
Maria Lopez
Chief Financial Officer | GridShift Energy
